events/kenya-province-1970/title: Church of the Province of Kenya inaugurated
events/kenya-province-1970/summary: The Anglican dioceses of Kenya, part of the Province of East Africa from 1960, became the separate Church of the Province of Kenya in 1970, with Festo Olang' as archbishop. It was renamed the Anglican Church of Kenya in 1998.
events/kenya-province-1970/causes/0: CMS mission begun by Johann Ludwig Krapf at Mombasa (1844)
events/kenya-province-1970/consequences/: Prominent role in Kenyan public life and in GAFCON
events/roe-v-wade-1973/summary: The US Supreme Court recognises a constitutional right to abortion. Catholic bishops oppose it immediately; many Southern Baptists initially accept a limited right, but by the late 1970s evangelicals join a broad pro-life movement. The decision was overturned in Dobbs v. Jackson (2022).
events/pca-founded-1973/title: First General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America
events/pca-founded-1973/summary: Conservative congregations leaving the southern Presbyterian Church in the United States held their first General Assembly at Briarwood Presbyterian Church, Birmingham, in December 1973, citing theological liberalism, women's ordination and a planned merger with the northern church.
events/pca-founded-1973/causes/0: Disputes over biblical inerrancy and the Westminster Standards
events/pca-founded-1973/causes/1: Opposition to union with the UPCUSA
events/pca-founded-1973/consequences/1: Joining and receiving of the Reformed Presbyterian Church, Evangelical Synod (1982)
events/lausanne-congress-1974/summary: Convened by Billy Graham, 2,700 evangelicals from 150 countries adopted the Lausanne Covenant, chiefly drafted by John Stott. Latin American voices such as René Padilla and Samuel Escobar pressed for social responsibility alongside evangelism; Ralph Winter introduced 'unreached people groups'.
events/uniting-church-in-australia-1977/: Formation of the Uniting Church in Australia

On 22 June 1977 the Methodist Church of Australasia, most of the Presbyterian Church of Australia and most of the Congregational Union of Australia joined to form the Uniting Church in Australia, on the Basis of Union agreed in 1971. About a third of Presbyterian congregations continued as the Presbyterian Church of Australia.
Ecumenical movement and shared mission in the outback (e.g. the Australian Inland Mission)
Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress (1985) and covenant with it (1994)
2009 constitutional Preamble acknowledging First Peoples' prior presence
events/church-of-nigeria-province-1979/t: Church of Nigeria becomes a separate province
events/church-of-nigeria-province-1979/s: The Nigerian dioceses of the Church of the Province of West Africa (formed 1951) became the separate Church of Nigeria in 1979, building on the CMS mission begun at Badagry and Abeokuta in the 1840s and the episcopate of Samuel Ajayi Crowther.
events/church-of-nigeria-province-1979/c: Rapid growth in the 'Decade of Evangelism' (1990s)
Leadership in the GAFCON movement from 2008
events/assassination-of-oscar-romero-198: Archbishop Óscar Romero of San Salvador, who had become an outspoken defender of the poor against the military regime, was shot dead while celebrating Mass on 24 March 1980. He was canonised in 2018 and is honoured across denominations as a modern martyr.
events/pcusa-reunion-1983/summary: The northern United Presbyterian Church in the U.S.A. and the southern Presbyterian Church in the United States, divided since the Civil War (1861), reunited at a General Assembly in Atlanta in June 1983.
events/pcusa-reunion-1983/causes/0: Civil War and slavery-era division of American Presbyterianism
events/pcusa-reunion-1983/causes/1: Decline of sectional identity and ecumenical commitments
events/pcusa-reunion-1983/consequences/1: Some conservative congregations moved to the PCA or the EPC
events/kairos-document-1985/summary: Black South African theologians in Soweto issued the Kairos Document, criticising 'state theology' that justified apartheid and 'church theology' that sought cheap reconciliation, and calling for prophetic theology. Alongside Desmond Tutu's leadership and the Belhar Confession, churches helped bring apartheid to an end.
events/kairos-document-1985/consequences: Church role in transition; Truth and Reconciliation Commission (1996)
events/elca-constituted-1987/title: Constituting convention of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America
events/elca-constituted-1987/summary: The American Lutheran Church, the Lutheran Church in America and the Association of Evangelical Lutheran Churches merged at a constituting convention in Columbus, Ohio (1987); the new church began operating on 1 January 1988.
events/elca-constituted-1987/causes/1: Departure of moderates from the Missouri Synod in the 1970s
events/elca-constituted-1987/consequence: Largest Lutheran church in the United States
Full-communion agreements with Reformed, Episcopal, Moravian and Methodist churches (1997–2009)
Departure of congregations to the LCMC and NALC after 2009 decisions on sexuality
events/lambeth-conference-1988/summary: Resolution 26 of the Lambeth Conference allows that a polygamist who responds to the gospel may be baptised with his believing wives and children, on condition that he takes no further wives and with the consent of the local Anglican community, while upholding monogamy as God’s will.
events/millennium-of-rus-1988/title: Millennium of the Baptism of Rus' and Orthodox revival
events/millennium-of-rus-1988/summary: Gorbachev permitted public celebration of the millennium of Rus' baptism, signalling an end to Soviet persecution. After 1991 thousands of churches and monasteries reopened across Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, though Orthodoxy's close ties to the Russian state became contested.
events/econe-consecrations-1988/summary: On 30 June 1988 Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre, founder of the Society of St Pius X, consecrated four bishops without papal mandate. The Holy See declared that Lefebvre and the four bishops had incurred excommunication and described the act as schismatic; the Society maintained that a state of necessity justified it in order to preserve Catholic tradition.
events/econe-consecrations-1988/causes/0: Opposition to aspects of Vatican II (religious liberty, ecumenism, collegiality) and to the 1969 Mass of Paul VI
events/econe-consecrations-1988/causes/1: Failed 1988 protocol between Lefebvre and Cardinal Ratzinger
events/econe-consecrations-1988/conseque: Motu proprio Ecclesia Dei (1988) and the founding of the Priestly Fraternity of St Peter
Remission of the four bishops' excommunications by Benedict XVI (2009)
Continuing doctrinal talks without full canonical regularisation
events/lausanne-spiritual-warfare-1993/s: Meeting in Nairobi, the Lausanne Committee’s Intercession Working Group issued a statement affirming the reality of spiritual warfare while warning against an unbiblical preoccupation with demons, against speculative “spiritual mapping” and against animistic or magical approaches, in response to the rise of strategic-level spiritual warfare.
events/lausanne-spiritual-warfare-1993/c: Growth of territorial-spirits teaching through the AD2000 movement
Became a reference point for evangelical critiques of strategic-level spiritual warfare
events/eritrean-autocephaly-1993/title: Eritrean Orthodox Church separates from the Ethiopian church
events/eritrean-autocephaly-1993/summary: After Eritrea's independence from Ethiopia (1993), the Coptic Orthodox Patriarchate under Pope Shenouda III agreed to the Eritrean church's autocephaly; Abune Philipos was consecrated as first Patriarch of Eritrea in Cairo in 1998.
events/eritrean-autocephaly-1993/causes/: Eritrean war of independence (1961–1991) and independence referendum (1993)
Desire for a national church distinct from the Ethiopian Patriarchate
events/eritrean-autocephaly-1993/consequ: Strained relations with the Ethiopian Orthodox Church
Later state involvement in the deposition of Patriarch Antonios (2006)
events/common-christological-declaration: Common Christological Declaration with the Assyrian Church of the East

Pope John Paul II and Catholicos-Patriarch Mar Dinkha IV signed a declaration recognising that Catholics and the Assyrian Church of the East confess the same faith in Christ, true God and true man, despite different terms (Theotokos vs 'Mother of Christ our God and Saviour'). It ended a division dating to 431 at the level of Christology.
Agreed Guidelines on Eucharistic admission with the Chaldean Church (2001)
events/toronto-blessing-1994/summary: From January 1994 meetings at the Toronto Airport Vineyard church led by John and Carol Arnott featured 'holy laughter', falling, shaking and animal-like noises interpreted as a refreshing of the Holy Spirit. Hundreds of thousands visited; John Wimber's Vineyard disaffiliated the church in 1995, and critics questioned the phenomena.
events/toronto-blessing-1994/consequence: Spread to Holy Trinity Brompton and globally
events/worldwide-church-of-god-reforms-1: The Worldwide Church of God embraces Nicene Christianity

After Herbert W. Armstrong's death (1986), the leadership of the Worldwide Church of God under Joseph W. Tkach re-examined Armstrong's teachings. The church adopted the doctrine of the Trinity (1993) and, in a December 1994 sermon, Tkach announced that Christians are not bound by Old Covenant laws such as the Saturday Sabbath, festivals and dietary rules. It is a rare case of a whole denomination moving into historic orthodoxy.
Study of Armstrong's teachings by the post-1986 leadership
Large splinter groups formed to keep Armstrong's teachings (United Church of God, 1995; Living Church of God, 1998)
Admitted to the National Association of Evangelicals (1997); renamed Grace Communion International (2009)
events/brownsville-revival-1995/summary: Beginning on Father's Day 1995 at Brownsville Assembly of God, evangelist Steve Hill's preaching on repentance launched nightly meetings over five years that drew an estimated 2.5 million visitors. Supporters reported conversions and restored lives; critics questioned manifestations and reported numbers.
events/lambeth-conference-1998/title: Lambeth Resolution I.10 on human sexuality
events/lambeth-conference-1998/summary: By 526 votes to 70, the Lambeth Conference upholds faithfulness in marriage between a man and a woman and abstinence for those not called to marriage, rejects homosexual practice as incompatible with Scripture, cannot advise blessing same-sex unions or ordaining those involved in them, and calls for pastoral care and listening to the experience of homosexual persons and condemnation of irrational fear of them.
events/lambeth-conference-1998/consequen: Consecration of Gene Robinson (2003) and ensuing crisis
events/exorcism-rite-revised-1999/summar: The Congregation for Divine Worship published De exorcismis et supplicationibus quibusdam (January 1999), the first revision of the 1614 rite, requiring that exorcists distinguish possession from psychiatric illness and use the rite with prudence and episcopal permission.
events/exorcism-rite-revised-1999/causes: Renewed demand for exorcism in Italy, Africa and the Americas
events/exorcism-rite-revised-1999/conseq: Dioceses later appointed more exorcists; the International Association of Exorcists was recognised in 2014
